license_note: Dimensional facts from published standards: ASME B1.1-2003 (Unified inch screw threads; basic profile, tensile stress area formula and tabulated values, also FED-STD-H28), ASME B18.2.8-1999 (clearance holes for bolts, screws and studs), ASME B18.3-2012 (socket cap screws: head dimensions, hex-key sizes, drill and counterbore table), ANSI/ASME B94.11M-1993 (number/letter/fractional twist-drill diameters), ASME B18.2.1 / B18.2.2 / B18.6.3 / B18.22.1 (hex cap screws, hex nuts, machine screw nuts, plain washers; related_hardware only), SAE J429 (mechanical properties of externally threaded fasteners), ASTM A574 (alloy-steel socket head cap screws), ASTM F837 / F593 (stainless steel socket screws / bolts). Tap drill selections (75% and ~50% thread) follow the conventional charts republished in Machinery's Handbook and by tap manufacturers; they are conventions, not normative requirements. Numbers were compiled from memory of those standards (network access to the standards bodies was blocked) and then cross-checked, at reconciliation, against the CSV data files of the open-source gumyr/cq_warehouse project (raw.githubusercontent.com, which was reachable): tap_hole_sizes.csv, clearance_hole_sizes.csv, socket_head_cap_parameters.csv, drill_sizes.csv. Where cq_warehouse and the reviewers' recall agreed against the compiler, the compiler's value was replaced. Every field carries a confidence label. Copyright in the standards documents belongs to the issuing bodies; the numeric values themselves are facts. cq_warehouse is Apache-2.0.

columns.key: thread designation, e.g. '1/4-20' (UNC) or '1/4-28' (UNF). Source: ASME B1.1-2003
columns.series: UNC or UNF. Source: ASME B1.1-2003
columns.major_in: in, basic major (nominal) diameter D. Source: ASME B1.1-2003 Table 1
columns.major_mm: mm, major_in x 25.4, rounded half-up to 3 decimals
columns.tpi: threads per inch n. Source: ASME B1.1-2003
columns.pitch_mm: mm, 25.4 / tpi, rounded half-up to 4 decimals
columns.minor_int_basic_in: in, basic minor diameter of the INTERNAL thread = D - 1.082532 P (P = 1/n). This is the diameter a CAD hole-wizard / cosmetic-thread feature should model for a tapped hole. Source: ASME B1.1-2003 basic profile (arithmetic)
columns.pitch_dia_basic_in: in, basic pitch diameter = D - 0.649519 P. Source: ASME B1.1-2003 basic profile (arithmetic)
columns.tap_drill_75: conventional tap-drill name for ~75% thread height (aluminium, mild steel, brass). CONVENTION, not a standard's fixed value. Source: Machinery's Handbook / tap-maker chart; matches gumyr/cq_warehouse tap_hole_sizes.csv 'Soft'
columns.tap_drill_75_in: in, diameter of that drill per ANSI/ASME B94.11M-1993
columns.tap_drill_75_thread_pct: %, thread height obtained with that drill = (D - drill) x n / 1.29904 x 100 (Machinery's Handbook formula), rounded to whole percent
columns.tap_drill_50: tap-drill name for the 'hard / tough material' column (~50-55% thread): stainless, titanium, deep holes > 1.5D. CONVENTION. Source: gumyr/cq_warehouse tap_hole_sizes.csv 'Hard' (bd_warehouse uses the same file); matches skeptic recall of the common chart
columns.tap_drill_50_in: in, diameter of that drill per ANSI/ASME B94.11M-1993
columns.tap_drill_50_thread_pct: %, thread height with that drill, same formula
columns.clearance_close: close-fit clearance drill name. Source: ASME B18.2.8-1999 Table 1 (recall) cross-checked gumyr/cq_warehouse clearance_hole_sizes.csv
columns.clearance_close_in: in, diameter of that drill per B94.11M (fractional drills are exact)
columns.clearance_close_nom_in: in, the nominal hole diameter as ASME B18.2.8 Table 1 states it (3 decimals); the named drill is the standard drill nearest to it
columns.clearance_normal: normal-fit clearance drill name (general default). Source: ASME B18.2.8-1999 Table 1 (recall) cross-checked cq_warehouse
columns.clearance_loose: loose-fit clearance drill name. Source: ASME B18.2.8-1999 Table 1 (recall) cross-checked cq_warehouse
columns.shcs_head_d_in: in, socket head cap screw head diameter A, MAX. null when the size is not in the B18.3 SHCS series. Source: ASME B18.3-2012 Table 1 (1960 series), cross-checked cq_warehouse socket_head_cap_parameters.csv asme_b18.3:dk
columns.shcs_head_h_in: in, SHCS head height H, MAX (= nominal diameter). Source: ASME B18.3-2012 Table 1
columns.shcs_hex_key: nominal hex socket / key size across flats, fractional inch, standard-head SHCS only (button, flat and low-head screws use smaller keys: see related_hardware). Source: ASME B18.3-2012 Table 1
columns.shcs_hex_key_in: in, decimal of the nominal key size
columns.cbore_d: nominal counterbore diameter for a standard SHCS, fractional inch. Source: ASME B18.3-2012 drill-and-counterbore table (recall; compiler and two skeptics agree). About head_d MAX + 1/16 in
columns.cbore_depth_min_in: in, MINIMUM counterbore depth to sink the head flush = shcs_head_h_in (MAX head height). CONVENTION: B18.3 does not tabulate a depth; add 0.010-0.030 in so the head sits below the surface
columns.tensile_stress_area_in2: in^2, As as tabulated in ASME B1.1-2003 Appendix B / FED-STD-H28 (3 significant figures; #4-40 tabulated 0.00604 vs formula 0.00603)
columns.tensile_stress_area_formula_in2: in^2, As = 0.7854 (D - 0.9743/n)^2 evaluated here to 5 decimals, so a reader can see how close the tabulated value is
columns.int_thread_shear_area_per_in_in2: in^2 per inch of engagement, INTERNAL thread shear (stripping) area ASn/Le = pi n Kn [1/(2n) + 0.57735 (Es - Kn)] (ASME B1.1 Appendix B / FED-STD-H28) evaluated at BASIC Kn (internal minor) and Es (pitch dia). The standard uses Kn MAX and Es MIN (class 2B/2A limits, not tabulated here), which gives a slightly smaller, more conservative area; treat this value as +/-10%
columns.int_thread_shear_area_per_mm_mm2: mm^2 per mm of engagement, the same quantity x 25.4
columns.related_hardware: object; SECONDARY data (hex cap screw, nut, washer, button-head and flat-head socket screws) each with its OWN confidence and source. NOT folded into the row confidence. All values are recall-grade: verify before cutting
columns.field_confidence: object mapping every top-level numeric/drill field of the row to certain | likely | recall (n/a for null fields)
columns.disputed: object, present only where reviewers disagreed on a value: lists the alternatives and who gave them
columns.confidence: row confidence = the MINIMUM of field_confidence over the top-level fields (related_hardware excluded). certain | likely | recall
columns.source: per-column provenance string for the row (same for every row; per-column detail is also in this 'columns' block)

rows.source: major/tpi/pitch/minor/pitch-dia: ASME B1.1-2003 basic profile; tap_drill_75: Machinery's Handbook 75%-thread chart (convention), cross-checked gumyr/cq_warehouse tap_hole_sizes.csv 'Soft'; tap_drill_50: gumyr/cq_warehouse tap_hole_sizes.csv 'Hard' (convention, ~50% thread); drill diameters: ANSI/ASME B94.11M-1993; clearance_*: ASME B18.2.8-1999 Table 1 (recall) cross-checked cq_warehouse clearance_hole_sizes.csv; shcs_*: ASME B18.3-2012 Table 1 (recall) cross-checked cq_warehouse socket_head_cap_parameters.csv; cbore_d: ASME B18.3-2012 drill-and-counterbore table (recall, three independent recalls agree); tensile_stress_area: ASME B1.1-2003 Appendix B formula, recomputed; int_thread_shear_area_per_in: ASME B1.1 Appendix B / FED-STD-H28 formula evaluated at BASIC dimensions

notes: USAGE. (1) TAP DRILLS. tap_drill_75 is the conventional ~75% thread-height chart for hand or machine cut-tapping in 6061-T6, mild steel and brass. tap_drill_50 is the 'hard material' column (~50% thread) for 300-series stainless, titanium, tool steel and any hole deeper than 1.5D: use it in stainless couplers and tank end caps or expect broken taps. Thread strength beyond ~60% engagement gains very little; a 50% thread in steel or stainless is stronger than a 75% thread in aluminium. Thread percentage for ANY drill (e.g. a substituted metric drill) is %(D - drill_in) x n / 1.29904 x 100; stay between 50 and 80. Form (roll) taps need a larger drill (roughly D - 0.5P) and are NOT covered. STI (Helicoil-type insert) tap drills are NOT supplied: they are roughly 0.3P over the nominal diameter (1/4-20 STI drill is 17/64 in, recall) but you must use the insert maker's chart. (2) CLEARANCE HOLES are ASME B18.2.8-1999 close/normal/loose. The compiled version of this table carried the widely republished hobby 'close/free' chart for the numbered sizes and an extrapolated +1/64,+1/32,+3/64 triple for 1/2 in; those were WRONG and were replaced (see reconciliation). Close fit is for CNC-matched patterns or dowel-like location; normal is the general default; loose is for hand-drilled parts or large stack-ups. The *_nom_in columns give the standard's nominal hole; the named drill is the nearest standard drill (e.g. #6 normal: nominal 0.170, drill #18 = 0.1695). For a bolted flight joint that must also locate (coupler bulkhead, motor retainer), do NOT use the bolt in a clearance hole for shear location; use dowel pins or a shoulder (press-fit dowel hole tolerances are in the dowel/press-fit table, not here). (3) SHCS head dimensions are MAX values from ASME B18.3-2012 (1960 series); the counterbore column is the B18.3 nominal counterbore, which is about head_d MAX + 1/16 in (for 1/4: 7/16 - 0.375 = 0.0625). B18.3 does not tabulate counterbore depth; cbore_depth_min = head height MAX puts the head flush, so add 0.010-0.030 in. Hex-key sizes in the main columns are for standard SHCS only; button-head and flat-head keys (smaller) are in related_hardware. Low-head SHCS keys are NOT supplied (not recalled with confidence). #12 is not a B18.3 SHCS size; its SHCS/counterbore fields are null. (4) STRENGTH. As = 0.7854 (D - 0.9743/n)^2. Minimum ultimate bolt load = As x UTS_min; recommended preload for a reusable joint is ~75% of proof load (J429 grades) or ~75% of 0.2% yield (A574/F837). Bolt SHEAR strength is commonly taken as 0.6 x UTS (likely; NASA RP-1228 / MIL-HDBK-5 practice) -- use it for rail buttons, fin brackets and thrust-loaded retainer screws in single shear. (5) THREAD ENGAGEMENT (the governing check in aluminium). Internal-thread stripping load = int_thread_shear_area_per_in x Le x Fsu(internal material). Le needed to develop the bolt = As x UTS_bolt / (int_thread_shear_area_per_in x Fsu). Fsu: 6061-T6 ~27 ksi (MMPDS, likely), 7075-T6 ~44 ksi (likely), 1018 ~40 ksi, 304 ~ 0.6 x UTS. Worked example, 1/4-20 A574 in 6061-T6: 0.0318 x 180 / (0.4615 x 27) = 0.46 in = 1.8D, which is why the rule is 1.5-2.0D in aluminium and 1.0D in steel, or use a threaded insert. The shear-area column is evaluated at basic dimensions; class 2B/2A minimum-material limits give ~5-10% less area. (6) TORQUE. T = K x F x d (T in lbf-in, F preload lbf, d nominal in). K = 0.20 plain/black-oxide steel dry, 0.15-0.17 lubricated or waxed, 0.12-0.14 with moly, 0.25-0.35 stainless-on-stainless dry (galls: ALWAYS anti-seize stainless). Example 1/4-20 A574 at 75% yield: F = 0.75 x 153 ksi x 0.0318 = 3650 lbf, T = 0.20 x 3650 x 0.25 = 180 lbf-in (K values: likely). Small screws in aluminium are limited by thread stripping, not bolt yield: check (5) first. (7) MATERIAL PROPERTIES (minimums; MPa = ksi x 6.894757). SAE J429 grade 5, 1/4-1 in: proof 85 ksi (586 MPa), yield 92 (634), UTS 120 (827), medium-carbon Q&T, 3 radial head marks [certain, SAE J429-2014]; 1-1/8 to 1-1/2 in: 74/81/105 ksi. SAE J429 grade 8, 1/4-1-1/2 in: proof 120 (827), yield 130 (896), UTS 150 (1034), alloy Q&T, 6 radial marks [certain, SAE J429-2014]. J429 grades start at 1/4 in; #2-#12 machine screws are NOT graded to J429. ASTM A574 alloy-steel SHCS (black oxide), up to and including 1/2 in: UTS 180 ksi (1241 MPa), 0.2% yield 153 (1055) [likely]; over 1/2 in: UTS 170 (1172), yield 144 (993) [recall; corrected from compiler's 153, which was a spot-check skeptic disagreement]; A574 also tabulates a proof-load stress of about 135-140 ksi [recall; the compiler's 'no proof load' statement was withdrawn]. Stainless SOCKET screws are ASTM F837 (not F593); F837 group 1 (18-8: 302/303/304) condition CW, 1/4-5/8 in: UTS ~100 ksi (689 MPa), yield ~65 ksi (448 MPa) [recall]; F593 CW group 1 has the same 100/65 ksi for 1/4-5/8 in hex bolts [likely]. Sizes BELOW 1/4 in and over 5/8 in are made to lower strength: vendors quote 70-90 ksi UTS for 18-8 machine screws and small SHCS [recall]; do not assume 100 ksi below 1/4 in. Austenitic stainless galls on stainless: anti-seize or a dissimilar nut for anything torqued repeatedly. (8) NYLON SHEAR PINS (rocketry separation joints; recall only, out of scope of the standards above): nylon 6/6 #2-56 screws shear at roughly 30-40 lbf, #4-40 at roughly 50-65 lbf, #6-32 roughly 100-120 lbf in single shear at room temperature; batch-to-batch and temperature scatter is large, so the club MUST pull-test its own batch and derate for cold. Use the #2-56 / #4-40 / #6-32 rows only for hole sizing (drill the shear-pin hole at the close or normal clearance value in BOTH parts). (9) SERIES. UNC is the default for tapped aluminium; UNF gives ~10-15% more As and finer adjustment but cross-threads and strips more easily in soft metal. Clearance, SHCS, counterbore and related_hardware depend only on nominal diameter, so UNC/UNF pairs share them. (10) UNITS/ROUNDING. All inch values are as the standards give them; mm values are conversions (x25.4) rounded HALF-UP to 3 decimals (pitch 4 decimals) and are NOT independent standard values. Exact-half cases therefore read 4.763 (3/16 in), 7.938 (5/16), 11.113 (7/16), 0.7938 (25.4/32). Do not 'round' a mm value back to a metric drill size without checking the thread percentage in (1). (11) CONFIDENCE. Row 'confidence' is the minimum over the row's top-level fields; 'field_confidence' shows which field is limiting. No row is 'certain' because tap drills are conventions and clearance/SHCS values are recall cross-checked against one open-source dataset, not against the printed standard. related_hardware blocks are all 'recall' and carry their own label. Nothing here was verified against the standards themselves (standards sites were unreachable); before the first cut of a flight part, spot-check the row against a printed Machinery's Handbook or the standard. (12) NOT SUPPLIED (reviewers asked; no confident source): low-head SHCS dimensions and keys; STI insert tap drills; class 2A/2B pitch/minor diameter limits; dowel/press-fit hole tolerances; UNF companions #2-64, #4-48, #6-40, #8-36 (rare in club hardware; tap drills #50, #42, #33, #29 respectively are recall-grade if ever needed). Rows dropped at reconciliation: none (no reviewer judged any row too uncertain to cut from once corrected).
